answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Requiring a longer lock as an account creates more identities makes Sybil farming expensive: an attacker must fund each account separately and cannot quickly recycle the same stake after detection. A trusted anchor can publish the lock rules, while a copper ledger records deposits and release dates at the wharf where agents register. The cost is capital tied up over time, plus the risk of losing stake for provable abuse.
